meta.title: Ch 6: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 6 (Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements).

questions.q: A major inspection component of a plant has a carrying amount of Rs 12 crore at the time of a subsequent major inspection, and the new inspection costs Rs 20 crore. Under Ind AS 16, the entity should:
o: Expense the new inspection and keep the old component
Capitalize the new inspection cost and derecognise the carrying amount of the replaced (previous inspection) component
Amortise the old carrying amount over the new inspection period
questions.why: Ind AS 16 requires capitalising the day-to-day repair expense as an expense, but for major inspections: capitalise the cost of replacing the inspection component and derecognise the carrying amount of the previous inspection part (even if it was not separately identified — estimate using cost of the new part adjusted for price changes and condition).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — replacement-parts derecognition is a recurring objective-paper theme AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: New inspection capitalised, old inspection part derecognised — no offsetting, no amortising ghosts. If not identifiable, back-solve old from new price-adjusted.
mem.link: Ch 6

questions.q: Residual value of an asset is revised upward such that it now EXCEEDS the asset's carrying amount. Ind AS 16 requires:
o: Immediate gain recognition for the excess
No further depreciation until residual value falls below carrying amount, with retrospective restatement of past charges
questions.why: Where residual value exceeds carrying amount, depreciation becomes zero (an asset is not depreciated below its residual value); the change is prospective as a change in estimate — past depreciation is not restated and no gain is booked.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — depreciation stop/start edge cases are classic traps Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Residual > carrying amount ⇒ depreciation pauses at zero; never book a profit or rewrite history — estimates move forward only.
mem.link: Ch 6

questions.q: During a year, total project spend was Rs 90 lakh; Rs 36 lakh relates to the research phase (whole year) and Rs 54 lakh to development, of which Rs 10 lakh was incurred before the recognition criteria were met in mid-year. The intangible asset capitalised is:
questions.why: Research spend (36) is expensed. Development spend before criteria met is also expensed (10); only post-criteria development (54 − 10 = 44) is capitalised. Once expensed, expenditure is never capitalised later.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the 'phase boundary' calculation appears in most attempts Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: R&D gate: research always P&L; development P&L until criteria met, then capitalise. Expensed is forever expensed.
mem.link: Ch 6

questions.q: Inventory of a model line (cost Rs 60 lakh) is held to fulfil a fixed-price contract. Contract selling price is Rs 75 lakh; costs to complete and sell Rs 8 lakh. Expected price of the model line WITHOUT the contract is Rs 50 lakh. NRV should be measured from:
o: Rs 50 lakh — market price always governs
Rs 75 − 8 = Rs 67 lakh — contract price is the appropriate basis
Average of contract and market price
Rs 60 lakh — cost is the floor
questions.why: Ind AS 2: inventory held to satisfy a sales contract — NRV is measured using the CONTRACT price; the general selling price is used only for quantities held in excess of the contract quantity. Here 67 > cost 60, so no write-down.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — dual-price NRV questions are a persistent RTP pattern AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Contract first, market for overflow. One inventory, two NRVs — split quantity before split price.
mem.link: Ch 6

questions.q: A property held by an owner-occupier for administrative use is reclassified when the owner vacates and begins leasing it out to generate rentals. Ind AS 40 requires the transfer to be measured:
o: At carrying amount (cost model) — carrying amounts equal fair value conceptually
Under the fair-value model, any change from carrying to fair value at date of transfer to P&L (increase) / P&L (decrease)
Only in OCI regardless of model
questions.why: For the fair value model, transfer from owner-occupied to investment property: difference at transfer date between carrying amount and fair value is treated like a revaluation (increase to OCI under 16, decrease to P&L). Under the cost model, carrying amounts simply move across.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the asymmetric P&L/OCI treatment is the discriminating option AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Fair-value model reclassification: gains behave like revaluation (OCI), losses hit P&L immediately. Direction decides the home.
mem.link: Ch 6

questions.topic: Ind AS 16 — fair value at transition
questions.q: Deemed cost for an item of PPE at Ind AS transition may be:
o: Its fair value at the date of transition
questions.why: Ind AS 101 permits fair value at transition date as deemed cost for PPE/intangibles (or revalued amount under prior GAAP with conditions).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — a transition freebie asked with regularity Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 16 — fair value at transition
mem.tip: Deemed cost at transition = fresh fair-value start; later Ind AS life begins with that stamp.
mem.link: Ch 14/Ch 6

questions.q: An intangible asset is considered to have an indefinite useful life when:
o: No analytical limit to the period of cash generation can be reliably determined
questions.why: Ind AS 38: indefinite life when no foreseeable limit to the period over which asset-generated cash flows are expected; amortisation skipped but annual impairment testing mandatory, with re-assessment each reporting period.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the amortise-vs-impair swap is the trap's heart AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Indefinite ≠ immortal: skip amortisation, submit to yearly impairment and a re-test of the label itself.
mem.link: Ch 6

questions.q: Which cost is INCLUDED in the initial measurement of an item of PPE under Ind AS 16?
o: Costs of abnormal waste during construction
questions.why: Included: purchase price (less rebates), directly attributable costs (site prep, delivery, installation, testing). Excluded: admin/general overheads, start-up/operating losses, abnormal waste, training.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — include/exclude lists generate easy Section B 1-markers AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Training teaches people, not machines — out. Testing confirms the asset — in. Ask: does the cost get the ASSET ready?
mem.link: Ch 6

questions.q: The gain or loss on disposal of an item of PPE is measured as:
o: Difference between net disposal proceeds and carrying amount, reported in P&L
Book value less salvage, in OCI
questions.why: Ind AS 16: derecognition gain/loss = proceeds less carrying amount, recognised in P&L when the item is disposed/retired (no OCI recycling of revaluation surplus to P&L on disposal — transfer within equity).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the gain-to-P&L vs surplus-to-equity split is repeatedly tested AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Disposal gain to P&L; the old revaluation surplus quietly slides to retained earnings — never parades through income.
mem.link: Ch 6

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the six cumulative criteria for capitalising development costs (Ind AS 38)?
o: Technical feasibility to complete the intangible
Availability of adequate resources to complete
Intention to use or sell the asset
questions.why: Six criteria: technical feasibility; intention to complete/use/sell; ability to use/sell; how probable future economic benefits; resources available; reliable measurement of expenditure. Auditor concurrence is not one.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the not-in-list format with an invented 'approval' distractor AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Six criteria, no auditor gatekeeping: feasibility, intention, ability, benefits, resources, measurement.
mem.link: Ch 6

questions.q: Capitalisation of borrowing costs is suspended while active development is interrupted for extended periods, unless:
o: The interruption is a necessary part of getting the asset ready
questions.why: Suspension during extended interruptions — except when the interruption is necessary to complete the asset (e.g., mandatory tests, flood waits in design).
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the exception-to-suspension is the trap AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Pause the clock only for true stalls — planned pit stops still tick interest.

questions.q: Gain or loss on issue, sale or redemption of an entity's OWN shares is:
o: Never recognised in P&L — equity movement
questions.why: Treasury and own-equity transactions never generate P&L gains/losses (Ind AS 32); share premium etc. sit in equity.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — own-shares-never-profit is an absolute Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: You cannot pay yourself from your own pocket and call it income.

questions.q: Costs of testing whether an asset functions properly are:
o: Capitalised as part of the asset cost
Offset by proceeds of items produced (e.g., sample sales) against cost
questions.why: Directly attributable costs include testing; net proceeds from items produced before intended use are deducted from the cost.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the sale-of-samples deduction is the trap AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Testing charges join the asset; sample sales pay the asset back — the cost is net of both.

questions.q: Borrowing costs capitalisation applies to own (equity) funds:
questions.why: Only the costs of BORROWINGS are capitalised; equity funds have no 'interest' to capitalise (though general-borrowing rates reflect opportunity within the rules).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the no-implicit-interest rule Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: No loan, no interest to carry; opportunity cost stays in economics, not in the asset.

questions.topic: Emphasis — no 20-year cap under Ind AS
questions.q: Under Ind AS 16/38 (as emphasised in the new scheme), useful life of an asset is:
o: Determined by the entity's expected pattern of consumption; no standard-imposed ceiling (Schedule III minima may apply for Companies Act formats)
questions.why: The old AS habit of a 20-year cap has no place in Ind AS 16/38 — the entity estimates; where the Companies Act Schedule II minima are followed for formats, Ind AS statements still reflect management's estimates per standards — an unlearning point the new syllabus stresses.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — first attempts reward teachers who fix inherited reflexes Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.ti: TI: Emphasis — no 20-year cap under Ind AS
mem.tip: Ind AS asks 'how long will you use it?', never 'what is the legal maximum?'
mem.link: Chapter 6 — Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

questions.q: Zenith Ltd holds inventory at cost Rs 155 lakh. NRV on the open market is Rs 137 lakh; a fixed-price contract covers all units at NRV Rs 167 lakh. Net write-down required when inventory is written to NRV (open-market basis) is:
o: No write-down (contract cover exists) but only for contracted quantity — if none here
questions.why: Where units are not contract-covered, NRV is market-based: write down 155 − 137 = 18 lakh to P&L. If a fixed-price contract covers the units, use the contract NRV — hence no write-down for contracted quantity.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — NRV vs contract-price selection appears in both MCQ and case formats AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Write to NRV; contract price used for contracted quantity only. Loss = cost − NRV.
mem.link: Chapter 6 — Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements
